articles.titulo: Innate immune memory of past hepatic injury promotes ischemic cardiac inflammation.
articles.autores: Zhang S, Zhang Y, … Zhan Z (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Hepatic disorders frequently coexist with cardiovascular diseases, leading to worsened prognosis. However, the mechanisms of inter-organ communication and the impact of historical hepatic injury await elucidation. Here, we report that the historical liver damage triggers long-term reprogramming of the innate immune system, biases hematopoietic stem cells differentiation toward myeloid fate, and aggravates inflammatory injury during myocardial infarction (MI). This immune memory is transmissible in bone marrow transplantation and parabiosis models. Injured liver-derived palmitic acid is responsible for the metabolic rewiring of cardiac macrophages during memory formation and establishes persistent epigenetic signatures in the transcriptional regulatory regions of hepatic injury-associated memory ("HepMem") genes containing the activator protein-1 motif. The HepMem monocyte/macrophages are expanded in liver-injured mice and potentiate the post-MI inflammatory cascades and adverse cardiac remodeling. Therefore, the innate immune memory links the past hepatic injury with MI, guiding the promising therapeutic approaches for the inflammatory cardiac comorbidities.

v6.implicacao: Imunidade & Memória Imune (priming-imune): modelo em que um lipídio (palmitato) instrui a memória inata por marcas de cromatina; referência direta para o mini-review de histonas e priming em mosquitos e para a pergunta de qual metabólito do repasto instrui o priming.
v6.resumo: Lesão hepática antiga reprograma de forma duradoura o sistema imune inato, desvia a diferenciação de células-tronco hematopoéticas para a linhagem mieloide e agrava a inflamação no infarto do miocárdio; a memória é transferível por transplante de medula e parabiose. O ácido palmítico do fígado lesado rearranja o metabolismo dos macrófagos cardíacos e fixa marcas epigenéticas em genes com motivo AP-1 (assinatura HepMem).
v6.metodo: Modelos murinos de lesão hepática seguida de infarto; transplante de medula e parabiose para testar transmissibilidade; análise de metabolismo e cromatina de macrófagos cardíacos (a partir do abstract).

articles.titulo: S1P1-mediated metabolic reprogramming promotes astrocytic mitochondrial dysfunction via histone lactylation in subarachnoid hemorrhage.
articles.autores: Zhang L, Pang J, … Jiang Y (13 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mitochondrial dysfunction is a central event in the pathophysiology of subarachnoid hemorrhage (SAH). Accumulating evidence has demonstrated that mitochondrial function is vulnerable to metabolic alterations. While the role of neuronal mitochondrial dysfunction in SAH pathology is firmly established, less is known about mitochondrial dysfunction in astrocytes, the key regulators of brain homeostasis, especially its potential regulation by metabolic reprogramming after SAH. Hence, we aimed to define the metabolic reprogramming and its potential role in mitochondrial dysfunction in astrocytes post SAH.
We established in vivo and in vitro models of SAH. Glucose uptake, lactate production, and extracellular acidification rate (ECAR) measurement were employed to profile the metabolic alterations in astrocytes after SAH. ATP level, mitochondrial membrane potential, mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (ROS) production, oxygen consumption rate (OCR), and transmission electron microscopy (TEM) were applied to assess the structural and functional integrity of astrocytic mitochondria. Lentivirus carrying short hairpin RNA (shRNA) and adeno-associated virus (AAV) were used to knockdown sphingosine-1-phosphate receptor 1 (S1P1) to explore the role of S1P1 in astrocytic metabolism switch. Additionally, ChIP-qPCR was utilized to elucidate the epigenetic mechanism of S1P1-mediated metabolic reprogramming in regulating the mitochondrial function of astrocytes post SAH.
We provided new evidence that astrocytes underwent metabolic switch with enhanced glycolysis in the early stage of SAH which was mediated by S1P1 through mammalian target of rapamycin/hypoxia-inducible factor 1ɑ (mTOR/HIF1ɑ) activation. Notably, enhanced glycolysis-derived lactate accumulation in astrocytes promoted mitochondrial dysfunction. Mechanistically, we found that the enhanced glycolysis facilitated mitochondrial fission factor (MFF) transcription by elevated H3K9la, resulting in excessive mitochondrial fission and subsequent mitochondrial dysfunction in the early stage of SAH.
Our findings demonstrate that S1P1-driven glycolysis enhancement promotes astrocytic mitochondrial dysfunction via histone lactylation and provide a potential therapeutic strategy for SAH.

v6.implicacao: Imunidade & Memória Imune: lactilação de histona como elo entre glicólise e cromatina, candidata a mecanismo metabólico-epigenético no mini-review de histonas e priming.
v6.resumo: Após hemorragia subaracnóidea, astrócitos passam a glicólise aumentada via S1P1 (mTOR/HIF1α); o lactato acumulado eleva H3K9la, ativa a transcrição de MFF e causa fissão e disfunção mitocondrial.
v6.metodo: Modelos in vivo e in vitro de HSA; ECAR, OCR, MET de mitocôndrias, shRNA/AAV contra S1P1 e ChIP-qPCR.

articles.titulo: Circadian Gating of Neuroimmune Memory: A Shared Persistence-and-Gating Hypothesis for Chronic Pain, Depression, and Postoperative Cognitive Dysfunction.
articles.autores: Song X, Feng M, … Luan Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chronic pain, depression, and postoperative cognitive dysfunction provide distinct settings in which inflammatory responses and persistent vulnerability may intersect. Evidence for specific cytokine, synaptic, and microglial mechanisms differs across these conditions and does not establish a single comorbidity mechanism. We examine whether circadian context influences the formation or later expression of neuroimmune memory. Circadian regulation of inflammatory responses and innate immune memory each have experimental support, while their coupling in disease-relevant microglia remains unresolved. Human BCG vaccination studies provide a peripheral timing-and-training precedent, which cannot be assumed to operate in the brain. We distinguish immune memory from ongoing inflammation, neuronal chromatin regulation, and sustained symptoms, and separate cell-autonomous microglial timing from rhythmic environmental inputs. The framework generates distinct tests of imprint formation, maintenance, recall, and reversal. A convincing test requires a resolved first challenge, control of initial inflammatory exposure and recall phase, and cell-resolved molecular measurements coupled to altered secondary-response function. Failure to reverse an established imprint would not exclude a role for timing during its formation. Perioperative studies offer a defined exposure but must distinguish delirium from longer-term cognitive decline. This evidence-calibrated hypothesis specifies what must be demonstrated before circadian interventions can be linked to prevention or modification of neuroimmune memory.

v6.resumo: Hipótese de persistência e gating circadiano da memória neuroimune em dor crônica e depressão (Neurosci Biobehav Rev). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Microglial SUCNR1 senses metabolic state to regulate whole-body homeostasis.
articles.autores: Repollés-de-Dalmau M, Asimakidou E, … Fernández-Veledo S (31 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Peripheral metabolic cues influence central energy control through incompletely understood pathways. Succinate, a Krebs cycle-derived metabolite elevated during nutrient excess and inflammation, signals via the G protein-coupled receptor SUCNR1; however, its central nervous system (CNS) role remains poorly defined. Using integrated mouse, human, and cellular approaches, we investigated how the succinate-SUCNR1 axis regulates peripheral energy balance in normal and high-fat diet states. Cerebrospinal fluid succinate dynamics were dissociated from plasma levels yet reflected systemic metabolic status, supporting a distinct central succinate compartment dynamically associated with peripheral metabolic state. Multi-omic and functional analyses identified microglia as the principal CNS targets of succinate, characterized by high SUCNR1 expression and functional dependence on this signaling pathway. Microglial Sucnr1 deletion altered peripheral energy regulation, conferring resistance to diet-induced metabolic stress while disrupting physiological energy balance, including leptin responsiveness and fasting-refeeding behavior. These findings establish the microglial succinate-SUCNR1 axis as a key immuno-metabolic mechanism linking systemic metabolic signals to the hypothalamic control of energy homeostasis.

v6.implicacao: Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo (imunometabolismo): um metabólito do ciclo de Krebs informa o estado nutricional a células imunes residentes do SNC sob dieta hiperlipídica; a pergunta é transferível ao SNC e aos hemócitos do mosquito após repasto HFHS.
v6.resumo: O succinato do líquor, dissociado do plasma, reflete o estado metabólico sistêmico, e a microglia é seu alvo principal no SNC via SUCNR1. A deleção de Sucnr1 na microglia deu resistência ao estresse metabólico por dieta rica em gordura e alterou a resposta à leptina e o comportamento de jejum/realimentação.
v6.metodo: Camundongos em dieta normal e rica em gordura, líquor humano, multiômica e ensaios funcionais em microglia, deleção condicional de Sucnr1 (a partir do abstract).

articles.titulo: When location makes oxidative stress lethal: mitoxyperilysis at the immunometabolic stress interface.
articles.autores: Zhang Y, Xia XP, Zhao L (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mitoxyperilysis is a proposed lytic death pathway in which oxidatively damaged mitochondria become membrane-lethal when retained at the plasma membrane. In founding models, TLR stimulation plus carbon restriction engaged MYD88-dependent innate signalling and BAX/BAK1/BID-dependent mitochondrial oxidative stress, while mTORC2-RhoA-actin remodelling prolonged peripheral mitochondrial retention. Mitoxyperiosis denotes prolonged mitochondria-plasma membrane association and localised oxidative membrane injury, whereas mitoxyperilysis denotes the subsequent plasma membrane rupture and lytic cell death. In these models, NINJ1 contributed to terminal rupture and LDH/HMGB1 release without being required for cell death. The damaging oxidant, physical tether, and mechanism linking local injury to membrane failure remain unresolved. Sepsis may reproduce upstream metabolic-redox conditions, but direct evidence for the complete spatial sequence in patient-derived cells is lacking. This review separates founding-model findings from disease-relevant observations and untested steps.

v6.resumo: Revisão que propõe a mitoxiperilise: mitocôndrias oxidadas retidas na membrana plasmática tornam-se letais; nos modelos fundadores, TLR mais restrição de carbono ativam MYD88 e BAX/BAK1/BID, mTORC2-RhoA-actina prolonga a retenção e NINJ1 contribui para a ruptura. Os autores dizem que oxidante, ancoragem e ligação entre dano local e falha de membrana seguem sem resolução.

articles.titulo: Cytosolic and Mitochondrial CaImaging in Drosophila Dopaminergic Neurons.
articles.autores: Inoshita T, Imai Y (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The ATP-producing organelle, mitochondrion, controls cellular or synaptic Ca2+ concentrations through temporal uptake of Ca2+ outside of the mitochondria. Although intracellular Ca2+ influx occurs during neuronal activity, a persistently higher concentration of intracellular Ca2+ is neurotoxic. Healthy mitochondria ensure rapid Ca2+ uptake, which is necessary for proper neuronal activity. Mitochondrial Ca2+ buffering activity decreases in aged or sick neurons. In this chapter, we will introduce our protocol for evaluating Ca2+ buffering activity through the mitochondria during neuronal activity of dopaminergic neurons.

v6.resumo: Capítulo de métodos para imageamento de cálcio citosólico e mitocondrial em neurônios dopaminérgicos de Drosophila (Methods Mol Biol). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Structural basis of CO2 valence coding in Drosophila
articles.autores: Javorski D et al. (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: In the olfactory system, glomerular sensory channels of single receptor identity support reliable odor recognition for appropriate approach or avoidance behaviors. For many olfactory stimuli, the assigned sensory value is innate but weighted by the internal state and previous experiences. How context-dependent modulation of innate valence coding supports distinct behavioral responses is poorly understood. Here we show that CO2 sensory information in Drosophila, intrinsically aversive but modified by attractive food signals, diverges from the canonical glomerular channel already in the antennal lobe via the polarized local interneuron LN23. LN23 relays sensory input via an extraglomerular CO2 pathway and manipulation of LN23 activity revealed a dominant role in CO2-induced avoidance behavior. The extraglomerular CO2 pathway projects to the posterior lateral protocerebrum (PLP) adjacent to the canonical Lateral Horn (LH) olfactory processing center and segregates into anatomically distinct valence channels. Connectome data together with functional characterization showed the convergence of parallel CO2 channels onto two interconnected 3rd order neurons which integrate additional sensory modalities via distinct mechanisms: while the glomerular CO2 pathway converge with food relay neurons onto separated dendritic domains of the PD5 interneuron in the LH, the extraglomerular pathways integrating CO2 information with antennal humidity and temperature modalities establish antagonistic inputs onto the PLP interneuron PV9. This early anatomical divergence of a defined olfactory channel followed by separated multimodal integration provides a structural basis for context-dependent valence coding and appropriate behavioral responses.

v6.resumo: Preprint estrutural sobre a codificação de valência do CO2 em Drosophila; versão listada em 18/11 de DOI de janeiro. Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Analysis of Dopaminergic Functions in Drosophila.
articles.autores: Inoshita T, Takemoto D, Imai Y (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dopaminergic (DA) neurons regulate various physiological functions, including motor function, emotion, learning, sleep, and arousal. Degeneration of DA neurons in the substantia nigra of the midbrain causes motor disturbance in Parkinson's disease (PD). Studies on familial PD have revealed that a subset of PD genes encode proteins that regulate mitochondrial function and synaptic dynamics. Drosophila is a powerful model of PD, whereby genetic interactions of PD genes with well-conserved cellular signaling can be evaluated. Morphological changes in mitochondria, along with dysfunction and degeneration of DA neurons, have been reported in many studies using Drosophila PD models. In this chapter, we will describe imaging methods to visualize mitochondria in DA neurons and to evaluate spontaneous neural activity of DA neurons in the Drosophila brain.

v6.resumo: Capítulo de métodos para análise de funções dopaminérgicas em Drosophila (Methods Mol Biol). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Neuronal activity regulates glycolysis to sculpt synaptic transmission
articles.autores: Theisen EK et al. (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Neuronal computation imposes rapid, localized changes in energy consumption, yet how energy production is regulated at such fine spatiotemporal scales is incompletely understood. Using two photon imaging of neuronal activity and energy metabolism in Drosophila , we show that neurons recruit glycolysis in less than a second, with cell-type and subcellular specificity. This coupling scales with neuronal activity and is regulated by AMP-activated protein kinase (AMPK). Activity-induced glycolysis is tightly correlated with presynaptic sites in cholinergic neurons, and is required for cholinergic but not glutamatergic neurotransmission. In cholinergic neurons, glycolysis supports both energetic demand and acetylcholine biosynthesis, with ATP citrate lyase linking these functions by both activating acetylcholine biosynthesis and disinhibiting glycolytic flux. These findings establish glycolysis as a previously unrecognized regulator of cell-type specific computation.

v6.resumo: Preprint em Drosophila (neurônios colinérgicos) sobre atividade neuronal regulando a glicólise e a transmissão sináptica. Classificado pelo título e pela categoria; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Rhodopsin 7 is an ancestral non-canonical photoreceptor that shapes light-responsive behavior.
articles.autores: Kirsch V, Reinhard N, … Senthilan PR (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Animals rely on light not only for vision but also to adapt behavior to their environment through non-image-forming pathways. In Drosophila, most rhodopsins mediate retinal image formation, but Rhodopsin 7 (RH7) is widely expressed in the brain and optic lobe, acting as a non-canonical light sensor reminiscent of mammalian melanopsin. We combined expression mapping, behavioral assays, and phylogenetic comparisons to investigate its function. RH7 detects temporal changes in luminance, guiding rapid behavioral responses, and regulating daily activity patterns. Flies lacking RH7 are less active during the dark phase, while strains with constitutively active RH7 show increased activity. Phylogenetic analyses suggest that RH7 is an ancient rhodopsin present across panarthropods, representing an intermediate between G protein-coupled receptors and specialized rhodopsins, highlighting a key step in the evolution of non-visual light perception. These findings show that RH7 functions as a melanopsin-like sensor, shaping behavior, and illuminating the origins of light detection.

v6.implicacao: SNC de mosquitos: RH7 é conservada em panartrópodes, logo existe nos culicídeos; pergunta aberta se participa dos ritmos de atividade e de repasto.
v6.resumo: A rodopsina 7 de Drosophila funciona como sensor de luz não canônico, semelhante à melanopsina, expresso no cérebro e no lobo óptico: detecta mudanças temporais de luminância, guia respostas rápidas e regula a atividade diária (moscas sem RH7 ficam menos ativas no escuro). A filogenia a coloca como rodopsina antiga presente em panartrópodes.
v6.metodo: Mapeamento de expressão, ensaios comportamentais e filogenia.

articles.titulo: Corpora amylacea and synaptic organization in the human brain analyzed by volume electron microscopy.
articles.autores: Cano-Astorga N, Merchan-Perez A, DeFelipe J (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The presence of corpora amylacea in the brain is a frequent finding in normal aging and in a broad spectrum of neurological disorders, yet the significance of these deposits for the organization of human cortical circuits remains unclear. Here, we combined complementary light and electron microscopy approaches to analyze temporal lobe epilepsy biopsy specimens with and without corpora amylacea. Samples containing corpora amylacea showed marked alterations in synaptic circuit microorganization, which were not restricted to areas of corpora amylacea accumulation but extended throughout the cortical tissue. These changes were characterized by neuronal loss, gliosis, reduced synaptic density, an increased proportion of inhibitory synapses, and larger synapses. Integration of these structural findings with clinical data from the same patients further supports the view that corpora amylacea are associated with disease-related pathological processes. Together, these findings provide a basis for understanding the potential significance of corpora amylacea in human brain circuit dysfunction and may help to inform future research studies focusing on disease mechanisms.

v6.resumo: FIB/SEM e TEM em biópsias de epilepsia do lobo temporal com e sem corpora amylacea: com elas, houve perda neuronal, gliose, menor densidade sináptica, maior proporção de sinapses inibitórias e sinapses maiores, em todo o tecido e não só junto aos depósitos.
v6.metodo: FIB/SEM e TEM de biópsias humanas, contagem e morfometria de sinapses.

articles.titulo: A short embedding protocol for diagnostic electron microscopy: long-term implementation and diagnostic outcomes in a high-volume clinical series.
articles.autores: Zhou H, Zhou XJJ (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epoxy resin polymerization is a lengthy step in tissue preparation for transmission electron microscopy (TEM). We evaluated whether reducing the polymerization step alone to 40 minutes at 120 °C, with upstream processing unchanged, could maintain diagnostic quality. The protocol has been the sole routine method in a high-volume, accredited clinical TEM laboratory for more than 10 years. Among more than 30,000 consecutive cases, no embedding-related diagnostic inadequacy was identified in consultant pathologist sign-out records. In a prospective, blinded, split-specimen comparison of renal biopsies, both pathologists scored 4 or 5 on every feature for both methods. Nearly all scores were at the upper end of the scale, indicating comparable performance but not establishing statistical equivalence. Glomerular basement membrane thickness was closely similar (mean difference -12.7 nm, ~4%), within measurement variability and below diagnostic detection thresholds. Because curing behavior depends on the resin formulation and oven conditions, local validation is required before implementation.

v6.implicacao: Ultraestrutura & Bioimagem: pode encurtar a inclusão de rotina em MET; amostras de volume com contraste pesado precisam de teste próprio antes de qualquer adoção.
v6.resumo: Reduzir só a polimerização da resina epóxi para 40 min a 120 °C, mantendo o processamento anterior, preservou a qualidade diagnóstica: em mais de 30.000 casos consecutivos não houve inadequação ligada à inclusão, e a espessura da membrana basal glomerular diferiu 12,7 nm (cerca de 4%) entre métodos. Os autores exigem validação local conforme a resina e o forno.
v6.metodo: Série clínica de mais de 10 anos e comparação cega de biópsias renais divididas.

articles.titulo: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development.
articles.autores: Wang X, Zeng J, … Zhang R (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission.

v6.implicacao: Malária / Plasmodium (plasmodium-celular): o parasito usa uma proteína metabólica do hospedeiro como estabilizador do citoesqueleto do gametócito, o que liga a composição do sangue à transmissão e sugere imunolocalização de Hb em gametócitos por MET como experimento próximo.
v6.resumo: Estruturas de crio-EM de partícula única dos microtúbulos subpeliculares (SPMT) de gametócitos de P. falciparum mostram hemoglobina humana associada a eles na forma de dímero, e não de tetrâmero. Perturbar os microtúbulos e trocar a isoforma de hemoglobina indicou que essa associação é necessária para organizar os SPMT e para a maturação do gametócito.
v6.metodo: Crio-EM de partícula única de SPMT isolados de gametócitos em desenvolvimento; farmacologia de microtúbulos e troca de isoforma de hemoglobina (a partir do abstract).

articles.titulo: Thermodynamic, Kinetic, and Structural Basis of Polyspecificity in the Malaria Sugar Transporter PfHT1
articles.autores: Paul A et al. (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum relies on the polyspecific sugar transporter PfHT1 for survival in diverse nutrient environments, making the molecular basis of its polyspecificity a potential avenue for antimalarial drug discovery. However, the structural, thermodynamic and kinetic basis of the emergence of polyspecificity in membrane transporters are not established in literature. Despite advances in AI for protein engineering, the design of selective/promiscuous membrane transporter proteins remains challenging as it requires connecting substrate recognition to the energetics of the transport cycle. Here, we examine the molecular origins of polyspecificity in PfHT1 transporter using molecular dynamics simulations of substrate transport and experimental validation of the key residues that tune specificity. From a structural viewpoint, we hypothesize that polyspecific membrane transporter contains flexible structural elements that could reshape the binding pocket in a substrate-dependent manner. For PfHT1, the cracking of the extracellular helix TM7b allows flexible reshaping of the binding pocket similar to the promiscuous enzymes. The thermodynamic signature of polyspecificity emerges in the form of the substrate dependent stabilization of transport-competent states. From a kinetic perspective, this stabilization asymmetrically alters transition kinetics and channels the flux through diverse conformational pathways that facilitate the conformational transitions from outward to inward facing states. To investigate the contribution of the underlying interaction network to sugar specificity, we used graph-attention learning to prioritize mutant transporters with distinct substrate preferences. Distinct glucose- and fructose-dependent growth phenotypes identify positions with differential effects on sugar utilization, providing functional evidence relevant to substrate specificity within the polyspecific transporter. Together, these findings support a mechanism in which structural, thermodynamic and kinetics observables connect polyspecificity to conformational energetics, kinetics, and structural plasticity.

v6.resumo: Preprint de biofísica do transportador de hexoses PfHT1 de P. falciparum; versão listada em 18/11 de DOI de setembro. Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: The heteromeric Plasmodium falciparum pantothenate kinase has only one active site and does not require Pf14-3-3I for activity.
articles.autores: Liu X, Spry C, Saliba KJ (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Coenzyme A (CoA) is an essential molecule for the intraerythrocytic stage of Plasmodium falciparum. Pantothenate kinase (PanK) catalyses the first step of the CoA biosynthesis pathway and functions as a homodimer in most organisms investigated thus far. P. falciparum possesses a novel heteromeric PanK complex composed of PfPanK1, PfPanK2 and Pf14-3-3I. Using a mutagenesis approach, we generated 10 PfPanK mutants and demonstrate that the PfPanK complex has only one functional active site, with both PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 required for activity by the complex. We also show that PfPanK2 is essential for normal intraerythrocytic parasite proliferation using a conditional knockdown system. 14-3-3 binding motifs generally contain a phosphoserine/threonine residue. Mass spectrometry analyses of phospho-peptide enriched, immunoprecipitated PfPanK samples revealed phosphorylation sites in both PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 that were additional to the previously reported sites. To investigate the role of specific sites in PfPanK1 and PfPanK2 that may be involved in Pf14-3-3I binding, five additional mutants were generated. Mutagenesis of four predicted Pf14-3-3I binding sites in PfPanK1 resulted in a significant reduction in the amount of Pf14-3-3I bound to the PfPanK complex. Heterologous expression of the PfPanK complex in an insect cell system yielded a small amount of soluble protein that assembled in situ into a functional complex. Combined results from heterologous expression and P. falciparum mutagenesis suggest that Pf14-3-3I may not be essential for PfPanK activity but may be important for stabilising the PfPanK complex.

v6.resumo: Pantotenato quinase heteromérica de P. falciparum tem um único sítio ativo e dispensa uma proteína acessória (JBC). Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Genome-wide identification and analysis of RNA secondary structures in response to glucose in Plasmodium falciparum.
articles.autores: Zhang Y, Zheng G, … Qi Y (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Food intake has a significant effect on systemic physiology. The growth, development and transmission of malaria-causing Plasmodium parasites rely on carbohydrate utilization, and parasites must rapidly adapt to fluctuating host glucose concentrations throughout their life cycle. However, the precise process by which Plasmodium parasites quickly react and adapt to glucose stress, in general, remains elusive. The goal of this investigation was to determine whether glucose starvation affects the RNA secondary structure of parasites.
In this study, we applied different short-term glucose stresses on parasites to determine the effect of host-derived glucose nutrients on the dynamics of parasite development and RNA secondary structures. We found that the S-type rRNA expression level in the low glucose-treated group was higher than that in the 2 mg/mL control group. The RNA-seq results indicated that glucose significantly affects the expression of genes involved in RNA-related processes, antigenic variation, transport processes, stimulus response, and DNA-related activities. Metabolomics studies also revealed that several types of sugar compounds exhibit a decrease in metabolic activity when subjected to a reduction in glucose supply. Via analysis of three glucose conditions, we identified the RNA secondary structures of more than 2,721 transcripts throughout the intraerythrocytic trophozoite stage. We discovered a positive correlation between mRNA structural flexibility (icSHAPE scores) and transcript abundance (RPKM values), demonstrating a direct association between RNA structural openness and steady-state mRNA levels. Our results revealed structural alterations in the entire transcriptome, including glucose transporters, metabolic enzymes, and the erythrocyte invasion protein family. These genes were mainly enriched in response to stimuli or preferential biological processes. The total number of genes with changes in icSHAPE scores in the UTRs was significantly greater for the 3' UTRs than the 5' UTRs. Furthermore, by comparing icSHAPE reactivity profiles across glucose conditions, we identified candidate cis-acting RNA motifs predominantly located within UTRs, whose structural flexibility changed rapidly in response to glucose fluctuation. We term these glucose-responsive RNA motifs, as they constitute promising regulatory elements for future research into post-transcriptional glucose sensing mechanisms.
Our findings clarify glucose stress-triggered remodeling of in vivo RNA secondary structure during the P. falciparum intraerythrocytic stage, reveal the functional relevance of structural dynamics in parasite environmental adaptation, and lay a foundational resource for future nutrient stress and post-transcriptional regulatory research. These findings show that glucose, the primary carbon source for parasite survival, modulates RNA secondary structural dynamics via nutrient-sensing cascades to modulate parasite proliferation and adaptive development, which offers clues for developing novel antimalarial therapies.

v6.implicacao: Malária / Plasmodium: resposta do parasito à glicose do hospedeiro, ponto de contato com a pergunta de estado metabólico do hospedeiro e competência.
v6.resumo: Em P. falciparum, a restrição curta de glicose alterou a estrutura secundária de RNA (icSHAPE) de mais de 2.721 transcritos no trofozoíto, com mais mudança em 3'UTR do que em 5'UTR e correlação positiva entre flexibilidade e abundância do mRNA. Propõem motivos de RNA responsivos à glicose como elementos reguladores.
v6.metodo: icSHAPE em três condições de glicose, RNA-seq e metabolômica.

articles.titulo: AIedes: a neural-network framework for modelling the distribution and abundance of Aedes albopictus in Europe
articles.autores: Biazzo I et al. (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Modelling the distribution and abundance of invasive species requires the integration of heterogeneous ecological surveillance data with environmental covariates and reproducible computational workflows. Aedes albopictus is an invasive mosquito species whose ongoing geographical expansion across Europe, driven by climate change, trade, human mobility and urbanisation, is increasing both ecological and public-health concerns. Accurate mapping of its distribution and abundance is therefore essential for monitoring, forecasting and targeted vector-control strategies. Here we present AIedes, a neural-network framework that predicts both the presence and weekly egg abundance of Ae. albopictus across Europe using climate variables and harmonised surveillance data. The model reproduces the large-scale spatial distribution of the species and captures fine-grained spatiotemporal variation in egg-laying activity. To support reproducible evaluation, the framework is trained and validated on newly harmonised, large-scale surveillance and climate datasets, which are publicly available together with the model implementation and code. These resources provide a consistent benchmark for comparing vector distribution and abundance models and offer an extensible workflow for ecological forecasting of invasive mosquito species in other regions where comparable data are available.

v6.resumo: Preprint de rede neural para distribuição e abundância de Ae. albopictus na Europa; versão listada em 18/11 de DOI de maio. Classificado pelo título; resumo não lido.

articles.titulo: Climatic Suitability and Disease Burden Divergence in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean Region.
articles.autores: Maher OA, Bellizzi S (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study investigates whether climate suitability predicts malaria and leishmaniasis burden in the WHO Eastern Mediterranean countries (2000-2023). Multi-linear regressions models. Climate suitability models were developed using ERA5 reanalysis data and ecological thresholds. Reported malaria and leishmaniasis cases were analysed alongside conflict intensity, health expenditure, and governance indicators. Panel regression and sensitivity analyses assessed explanatory power. Climate suitability showed weak or negative correlations with reported cases, whereas conflict intensity and governance indicators demonstrated substantially stronger statistical associations and explained up to four times more variance in reported disease burden. In Syria, leishmaniasis incidence rose >15-fold during the civil war despite minimal climatic change. Surveillance disruptions in conflict-affected settings may contribute to underreporting, although the magnitude of this effect could not be directly quantified. Sensitivity analyses indicated that the study's main conclusions remained robust across a range of plausible underreporting assumptions. Climate appears to define ecological boundaries of transmission, whereas socio-political fragility is more strongly associated with variation in reported disease burden across countries and over time. Climate-only models are insufficient in fragile states; vulnerability and stability metrics must complement climate indicators in policy frameworks.

articles.titulo: Temporal analysis using machine learning of morbidity and mortality from vector-borne diseases in Brazilian municipalities.
articles.autores: Nicomedes NP, Costa AS, … Silva DCDCE (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study examined morbidity and mortality from four vector-borne diseases-dengue, yellow fever, leishmaniasis, and malaria-in Brazilian municipalities from 1999 to 2022. Rates were compared between eight triennia (Kruskal-Wallis, Dunn post-hoc) and tested for monotonic trend (Mann-Kendall, Theil-Sen) at national and municipal levels. Because the four diseases differ in vector and transmission ecology, a separate Random Forest was estimated for each disease-outcome combination on the full 1999-2022 municipality-year panel, under a common covariate set, with calendar year as a categorical split variable and covariates standardized within each year; importance uncertainty was estimated by resampling municipalities as clusters. Temporal patterns were heterogeneous, malaria declined consistently in both morbidity and mortality, dengue mortality increased monotonically, dengue morbidity rose in 16.5% of municipalities without a monotonic national trend, yellow fever was confined to the 2017-2018 sylvatic epidemic, and leishmaniasis showed no trend. Municipalities with extreme rates were concentrated in the North, Northeast, and Central-West, regions combining rapid urban growth, social vulnerability, and environmental degradation. Predictive performance was negligible, out-of-bag R2 ranged from -0.03 to 0.08 and fell to -0.05 to 0.02 under cross-validation grouped by municipality, so variable importance is reported as a ranking within low-performing models, not as evidence of prediction or causation. On that basis, the urbanization index was the covariate most frequently ranked first, followed by population density and CO2 emissions. The framework provides a descriptive basis for targeting surveillance under the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs 3, 10, and 13).

Os random forests tiveram desempenho preditivo desprezível (R² fora da amostra de -0,03 a 0,08), então a importância das variáveis (urbanização primeiro) é só descritiva.

articles.titulo: Spatiotemporal modeling of climatic effects on dengue transmission across Mexican municipalities.
articles.autores: Babasola O, Peter OJ, … Oshinubi K (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Dengue remains one of the fastest expanding mosquito borne viral diseases, with transmission strongly influenced by climatic conditions. In Mexico, recurrent dengue outbreaks show substantial geographic variation across municipalities, yet the extent to which climatic variability and spatial dependence contribute to this heterogeneity remains insufficiently understood. This study examined the spatiotemporal distribution of dengue incidence across Mexican municipalities and quantified associations with climatic variability and spatial dependence using a hierarchical spatial model. Municipality level surveillance data were compiled into a weekly panel of confirmed dengue cases and linked with gridded temperature, rainfall, and relative humidity data. Temporal relationships were assessed using weekly national time series and lagged correlation analysis, while spatial dependence was evaluated using Moran's I statistics. A negative binomial regression model with conditional autoregressive spatial random effects was used to estimate associations between dengue incidence and contemporaneous climatic conditions, with additional adjustment for population density. The results showed pronounced seasonal and interannual variation in dengue incidence, with climatic variables exhibiting distinct temporal associations with dengue activity. Significant positive spatial autocorrelation was observed throughout the study period, with elevated dengue burden concentrated primarily along the Gulf of Mexico, the Yucatán Peninsula, and parts of the Pacific coast. The spatial model showed positive associations of temperature and population density with dengue incidence, while substantial residual spatial variation remained after adjustment for the measured covariates. These findings indicate that climatic, demographic, and spatial processes contribute to geographic variation in dengue transmission across Mexico and support spatially explicit approaches for targeted surveillance and prevention.

articles.titulo: An actionable field practice integrated with real-time quantitative vector surveillance for precision intervention during the 2025 Chikungunya outbreak in Foshan.
articles.autores: Guo X, Chen H, … Chen XG (23 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Following the activation of Level III emergency response, China's grassroots public health systems, exemplified by initiatives like the Patriotic Health Campaign and community-based prevention networks, can be rapidly mobilized. To enhance precision in controlling China's first large-scale chikungunya fever outbreak in Shunde, Foshan, Guangdong Province, real-time quantitative surveillance was implemented. Real-time quantitative surveillance was conducted using MS400 traps and Intelligent Mosquito Ovitraps (IMTs) to monitor Aedes mosquito populations. These tools established a rapid monitoring network in Foshan, enabling daily data reporting with high spatiotemporal resolution. During comprehensive and targeted vector control phases, real-time data from MS-400 and IMT informed adaptive adjustments in local control strategies, optimizing resource allocation and intervention timing. This integrated field practice combining advanced surveillance technologies with community mobilization validates a scalable framework for precision Aedes-borne disease control, yielding actionable insights into mitigating emerging arboviral threats in resource-limited settings.

articles.titulo: Staggered cryo-plasma FIB milling enables high-throughput cryo-ET.
articles.autores: Lisicki E, Taubitz T, … Tacke S (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Cryo-focused ion beam (cryo-FIB) milling combined with cryo-electron tomography (cryo-ET) is a crucial technique for studying macromolecules in their native environment. To mill thick samples, plasma ion sources are used. However, the practicality of high plasma currents, which offer the greatest potential for increasing throughput, and their possible damaging effects on the sample have not yet been investigated. Here, we systematically examine high-current xenon plasma-FIB (PFIB) milling and quantify the current-dependent damage in over 4700 tomograms by preparing a total lift-out volume of 9000 µm³. We find that currents of up to 2500 nA can be used in cryo-ET lamella preparations, enabling increased milling speeds and sample volumes that can be examined while maintaining sample integrity. We demonstrate this using a newly developed high-throughput staggered milling routine for waffle-like preparations, in which we achieve high-resolution reconstructions of yeast ribosomes, and for tissue serial lift-outs, enabling a complete experiment within 24 hours. Our results and approach provide a strong foundation for future in situ structural investigations of medically relevant protein complexes in organoids, tissues, or entire organisms.

Uma rotina escalonada para preparos tipo waffle e lift-outs seriados de tecido permite um experimento completo em 24 h, com ribossomos de levedura em alta resolução.

articles.titulo: Chikungunya virus: from global emergence to immunopathology and therapeutic frontiers.
articles.autores: Li D, Wang Q, … Zhang S (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), a re-emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus, has transitioned from an endemic pathogen to a global public health threat. In May 2026, the World Health Organization's second rapid risk assessment classified the global public health risk of CHIKV transmission as moderate. Although two vaccines (IXCHIQ® and VIMKUNYA®) have been authorized in selected countries, no antiviral therapy has been approved, and supportive care remains the mainstay of clinical management. We synthesize current knowledge of CHIKV epidemiology, replication, host immune signaling, and immune evasion, together with the developmental landscape of vaccines and antivirals. Through a critical appraisal of available evidence, we propose a hierarchical evidence-weighting framework that distinguishes in vivo mechanistic findings, cell-line observations, and human validation, and we highlight the stage-dependent functions of cytokines. Finally, we outline unresolved questions in chronicity, antiviral development, next-generation vaccine design and optimization, and cross-regional public health coordination, with particular emphasis on bridging the evidence gap between animal models and human infection.

articles.titulo: Emerging orthobunyaviruses: genomic diversity, reassortment, and expanding public health risks.
articles.autores: Sankhe S, Ndiaye NA, … Diagne MM (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Orthobunyaviruses (family Peribunyaviridae) represent one of the most diverse groups of arboviruses, infecting humans, livestock, and wildlife worldwide. Despite their broad geographic distribution and ecological complexity, most orthobunyaviruses remain poorly characterized, with limited understanding of their genomic diversity, transmission dynamics, and pathogenic potential. While research has focused on clinically recognized viruses such as Oropouche virus (OROV), La Crosse virus (LACV), Jamestown Canyon virus (JCV), and Schmallenberg virus (SBV), numerous neglected lineages like Ilesha virus (ILEV), Bwamba virus (BWAV), and Ingwavuma virus (INGV) continue to circulate silently, particularly in Africa, Asia, and Latin America. Recent outbreaks of OROV in South America and the emergence of SBV in Europe highlight their capacity for rapid spread and significant public and animal health impact. The segmented negative-sense RNA genome of orthobunyaviruses enables reassortment, a key evolutionary mechanism that drives diversification and may generate strains with altered virulence or host range. In addition, climate change, environmental disruption, and increased human-animal-vector interactions may facilitate expansion into new regions. This review synthesizes current knowledge on taxonomy, evolution, ecology, clinical features, diagnostics, and surveillance strategies. We emphasize the importance of integrated genomic monitoring and One Health approaches to strengthen preparedness against emerging and neglected orthobunyaviruses.

articles.titulo: Serum untargeted metabolomics reveals infection-associated metabolic alterations in chikungunya, dengue, and influenza A virus infections.
articles.autores: Ouyang F, Chen X, … He M (8 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Chikungunya virus (CHIKV), dengue virus (DENV), and influenza A virus (IAV) infections may present with overlapping febrile symptoms during the early clinical phase. Routine laboratory tests provide useful clinical information but do not fully capture the circulating metabolic alterations associated with different viral infections. This study aimed to characterize serum metabolic profiles in CHIKV, DENV, and IAV infections using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics.
In this comparative cross-sectional study, serum samples from patients with CHIKV, DENV, or IAV infection and healthy controls were analyzed using liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS)-based untargeted metabolomics. Data were acquired in both positive and negative electrospray ionization modes, and the datasets were processed to characterize infection-associated metabolic alterations. Quality-control assessment, principal component analysis, orthogonal partial least-squares discriminant analysis, differential metabolite screening with Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate correction, Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) pathway classification, and receiver operating characteristic analysis were performed.
Thousands of metabolic features were detected across positive and negative ion mode datasets, and annotated features were retained for downstream comparative analyses. Principal component analysis revealed group-dependent metabolic clustering with partial overlap between healthy controls and viral infection groups. Compared with healthy controls, 319, 300, and 295 differential metabolic features were identified in the CHIKV, DENV, and IAV groups, respectively, in positive ion mode, whereas 52, 40, and 33 differential features were identified in negative ion mode. Downregulated features predominated in the positive-ion comparisons, while the direction of metabolic alterations varied across groups in negative ion mode. KEGG pathway classification showed that differential metabolites were mapped to several major categories, including lipid metabolism, amino acid metabolism, metabolism of cofactors and vitamins, xenobiotics biodegradation and metabolism, and chemical structure transformation maps. Exploratory receiver operating characteristic (ROC) analysis within the discovery cohort identified multiple metabolites with high discriminatory performance for distinguishing viral infection groups from healthy controls, although these findings were not independently validated. Additional mode-specific analyses further characterized shared differential metabolic features, their directional changes, and the distribution of candidate metabolites with high AUC values.
CHIKV, DENV, and IAV infections were associated with broad serum metabolic alterations compared with healthy controls. The CHIKV-versus-control comparison yielded the largest number of altered metabolic features in the current dataset, although this observation should be interpreted cautiously because of unequal sampling proportions and the absence of direct comparisons between infection groups. Given the relatively small sample size, single-center and single-outbreak design, and lack of an independent validation cohort, the candidate metabolites identified in this study should be regarded as exploratory and require validation in larger independent cohorts and targeted metabolomic assays.

Coorte pequena, de um centro e sem validação independente.

articles.titulo: Microbial Shifts in Metisa plana (Lepidoptera: Psychidae) Larvae Exposed to Bacillus thuringiensis and Flubendiamide.
articles.autores: Maidin MST, Hashim AM, … Jamian S (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Microbial communities in the insect body, especially in the gut, are crucial for host development, health, and environmental adaptation. However, little is currently understood about how these communities react to anthropogenic stressors, particularly when pesticides are used. This study aims to investigate the independent and synergistic effects of the biopesticide, Bacillus thuringiensis MPOB Bt1 (MPOB Bt1) and the synthetic diamide insecticide, flubendiamide (Fbd) on the microbial community of the oil palm bagworm, Metisa plana larvae. Larvae were collected at zero (DAT0), one (DAT1), and three days (DAT3) post-treatment and analyzed for bacterial genus abundance and network responses using shotgun metagenomic-derived taxonomic profiling. Analysis of larval microbial community shifts showed that the combined MPOB Bt1-Fbd treatment resulted in a significant increase in microbial richness, with network density rising from 0.1354 at DAT0 to 0.2279 at DAT3 compared to the individual Fbd treatment. Pearson correlation analysis also showed that the combined MPOB Bt1-Fbd treatment was associated with the growth of the microbiome members that can co-occur with Bacillus. The positive co-occurrence patterns between Bacillus and the genera Enterobacter and Pseudomonas in the combined MPOB Bt1-Fbd treatment may reflect treatment-associated microbial shifts during dysbiosis, with their ecological and functional relevance requiring further investigation. This preliminary study provides insights into microbial community responses to the mixture of MPOB Bt1-Fbd compared to the individual treatments. Further functional analysis of the microbial community is needed to clarify the potential roles of these taxa in pathogenicity, treatment response, and pesticide tolerance in the development of M. plana control methods in the future.
