articles.titulo: Spatiotemporal analysis of insecticide-treated bednet coverage, age and type in Africa from 2006-2024.
articles.autores: Tan E, van den Berg M, … Gething PW (9 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Since their rapid adoption from the mid 2000s, insecticide-treated nets (ITNs) have been one of the most impactful malaria interventions in Africa. Facing insecticide resistance and ever-increasing resource constraints, there is a growing need to revise previous modelling efforts of ITN coverage to better reflect the current epidemiological reality. Comprehensive estimates of ITN coverage must account for factors such as net type, net age, and user behaviours. By leveraging improved data availability, we propose a mathematically rigorous ITN coverage model that extends previous national-level models to the subnational level across 44 countries in Africa. The presented Multitype-ITN (MITN) model is used to construct longitudinal estimates of net demography by age and type from 2006-2024, and provide insights on potential sources of ITN distribution inefficiencies. Our findings show a significant increase in the uptake of next-generation ITNs, reflecting an increasingly diverse market. However, longitudinal trends suggests stagnation in key metrics of net coverage (nets-per-capita, access and use), alongside a downwards trend in utilisation - number of users per net, coupled with observed stationary use rates - proportion of people with access that also use nets. There are also early signs of interventions failing to meet the demands of increasing populations.

articles.titulo: The myokine irisin: role in the regulation of adipose tissue homeostasis and potential in the treatment of obesity.
articles.autores: Gisina AM, Lupatov AY, Yarygin KN (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Obesity is a global health issue that, in the modern world, affects children and adolescents as well. It is a chronic disease accompanied by metabolic disturbances such as insulin resistance and dyslipidemia. Obesity is characterized by low-grade chronic inflammation of adipose tissue, with the blood showing elevated levels of pro-inflammatory factors and reduced levels of anti-inflammatory factors - collectively known as adipokines - secreted by this tissue. Obesity contributes to the development of type 2 diabetes mellitus and increases the risk of atherosclerosis, hypertension, and other cardiovascular diseases. Skeletal muscles play a vital role in regulating systemic metabolism, partly through the secretion of biologically active factors called myokines. One such myokine, currently the subject of active research, is irisin, which is involved in the homeostasis of adipose tissue. Irisin is a peptide derived from the precursor protein FNDC5, produced primarily in striated muscle in response to physical exercise. Irisin participates in the regulation of carbohydrate and lipid metabolism, influences metabolic processes in the liver and skeletal muscle, stimulates thermogenesis, and is capable of modulating the remodeling of the immuno-metabolic microenvironment within adipose tissue. Increasing blood irisin levels through the administration of exogenous irisin is currently being explored as a potential therapeutic approach for obesity and associated cardiometabolic disorders.

articles.titulo: Role of Selected Myokines and Mineral Metabolism in Spinal Muscular Atrophy: A Systematic Review.
articles.revista: FASEB journal : official publication of the Federation of American Societies for Experimental Biology
articles.autores: Gryczyńska W, Gajewska E, … Skrypnik D (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Despite substantial progress in understanding spinal muscular atrophy (SMA), the roles of several biological factors in its pathophysiology remain incompletely characterized. This systematic review aimed to synthesize the current evidence on the role of selected myokines, namely myostatin, follistatin, IL-6 (Interleukin-6), and IGF-1 (Insulin-like growth factor 1), as well as the minerals, copper, zinc, calcium, iron, and magnesium, in the pathogenesis and treatment of SMA. A PROSPERO-registered systematic review included 25 studies. Risk-of-bias assessment using validated tools revealed heterogeneity in methodological quality. The findings suggested that reduced levels of myostatin were associated with disease subtype, functional status, but not with age or 30 months of nusinersen treatment. Follistatin demonstrated protective effects on the neuromuscular system in preclinical models, whereas clinical evidence was inconclusive, with no consistent associations with SMA subtype, age, or body weight. Altered IL-6 levels in blood samples from both children and adults were linked to neuroinflammatory processes and disease activity, suggesting its potential as a biomarker of treatment response. Exogenous IGF-1 attenuated muscle atrophy and improved motor function in preclinical models. Disturbances in mineral homeostasis were related to skeletal and metabolic dysfunction. Studies revealed reduced bone mineral density, magnesium and iron deficiencies, a relationship between copper metabolism and adverse body composition, and the potential neuroprotective role of zinc. Growing evidence suggests that "myokine-mineral crosstalk" may bridge neuromuscular integrity with bone remodeling and calcium-phosphate metabolism in SMA. Overall, these findings provide broader insights into the biological mechanisms underlying SMA pathophysiology and disease monitoring while emphasizing the need for a multidisciplinary research approach.

articles.titulo: Cryptic viruses shape trophic networks after biological invasions
articles.autores: Perez-Rodriguez J et al. (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Biological invasions restructure ecological communities by bringing previously isolated organisms into contact, but the viral flow within the trophic network and its consequences have not been established. Here, we show viral exchange following the introduction of a parasitoid wasp released for classical biological control in citrus. Within a few years, viruses spread bidirectionally between native and exotic host-parasitoid trophic chains and reached a generalist hyperparasitoid at the fourth trophic level. Cohabitation and multiparasitism, two ubiquitous interactions between the two trophic chains, were sufficient for viruses to be transferred between species and maintained transgenerationally. A virus acquired by the introduced parasitoid increased its offspring production by 30%. Our results identify cryptic viruses as an overlooked dimension of biological invasions, reshaping trophic networks and the outcome of the species we deliberately introduce.

articles.titulo: Immunopathological mechanisms linking atherosclerosis and ischemic stroke: From microenvironmental vulnerability to precision therapeutics.
articles.autores: Liu W, Zou Q, … Huang Z (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Atherosclerotic ischemic stroke results from a multistage process in which systemic susceptibility and local arterial biology converge to generate plaque vulnerability, thrombosis, embolization, and cerebral ischemia. This review critically integrates experimental, human tissue, observational, imaging, and randomized clinical evidence across this continuum. We distinguish disturbed flow-induced endothelial dysfunction and intimal retention of apolipoprotein B-containing lipoproteins as upstream processes from macrophage dysfunction, defective efferocytosis, vascular smooth muscle cell remodeling, pathological neovascularization, and intraplaque hemorrhage that promote structural vulnerability. We then examine how plaque rupture and, with less direct cerebrovascular evidence, superficial erosion interact with platelet activation, coagulation, and neutrophil-associated immunothrombosis to produce artery-to-artery embolization or hemodynamic ischemia. Systemic modifiers, including clonal hematopoiesis, trained immunity, gut-derived metabolites, psychological stress, infection, and environmental exposures, are evaluated according to evidence maturity and stroke-specific relevance. Poststroke neuroimmune-hematopoietic reprogramming is considered an experimentally supported but incompletely validated feedback mechanism in humans. Among imaging-defined plaque features, carotid intraplaque hemorrhage has comparatively mature human prognostic evidence, whereas many molecular signatures remain investigational. Emerging single-cell, spatial, multiomic, molecular-imaging, and thrombus-profiling technologies are considered separately from clinically validated risk tools. Finally, therapeutic strategies are organized by mechanism and strength of clinical evidence, distinguishing established lipid-lowering, antithrombotic, and reperfusion approaches from investigational inflammatory, lipoprotein(a)-directed, and genome-editing strategies. This evidence-based framework identifies where mechanistic insight is mature, where translation remains uncertain, and how precision prevention may be advanced in atherosclerotic stroke. SIGNIFICANCE STATEMENT: Atherosclerotic ischemic stroke is driven by more than arterial narrowing: plaque vulnerability, immune inflammation, thrombosis, and impaired cerebral perfusion interact to determine clinical risk. By separating findings supported by human cerebrovascular evidence from emerging experimental mechanisms, this review clarifies opportunities and limitations for improved risk stratification, biomarker development, and mechanism-guided prevention.

articles.titulo: [Spatiotemporal pathogenesis evolution of lung precancerous lesions from perspective of "immunometabolic" crosstalk and construction of framework for syndrome differentiation and treatment].
articles.revista: Zhongguo Zhong yao za zhi = Zhongguo zhongyao zazhi = China journal of Chinese materia medica
articles.autores: He JW, Huang CX, … Ma Q (11 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The imbalance of "immunometabolic" crosstalk is the core mechanism underlying the initiation and progression of lung precancerous lesions. Its essence lies in the spatiotemporal coupling and systemic interaction between metabolic reprogramming and immune response dysregulation across multiple stages and scales. The interweaving and iteration of these two processes manifest as a spatiotemporal pattern of pathogenesis evolution: "depression→phlegm→stasis→toxin". The stagnation of sweat pore and constraint of Qi movement provide the initial impetus for lesion onset and development; the blockage of triple energizer with coalesced phlegm and stasis forms the material basis of the substantive mass; and the malnourishment of the lung with accumulation and coalescence of toxin supplies the energy source for malignant transformation. Accordingly, this paper proposed the treatment principle of spatiotemporal integrated intervention with dynamic regulation, established the treatment sequence according to temporal progression, and directed the medicinal action according to the disease location level, thereby forming a spatiotemporal syndrome differentiation and treatment protocol aligned with the "depression→phlegm→stasis→toxin" evolution. In the temporal dimension, the focus for each stage was provided: during the depression stage, unblocking sweat pore to relieve constraint and dredge Qi movement; during the phlegm stage, harmonizing triple energizer to resolve phlegm and dissipate mass; during the stasis stage, dissipating mass, eliminating latent pathogenic factors, expelling blood stasis, and dredging collaterals; during the toxin stage, reinforcing healthy Qi, consolidating the lung, and eradicating toxin from its source. In the spatial dimension: wind-extinguishing medicinals were skillfully employed to open sweat pore and relieve constraint; warming medicinals were heavily used to resolve phlegm and harmonize the middle; insect medicinals were adeptly utilized to navigate the collaterals and eliminate latent pathogens; and targeted medicinals were specifically applied to directly suppress the root toxin. Clinically, these stages often intertwine and evolve dynamically. Therefore, a flexible approach to syndrome differentiation and treatment was essential to achieve the goals of regulating Qi movement, eliminating mass, reversing disease progression, and truncating transmission. Ultimately, this approach established a comprehensive framework for the spatiotemporal syndrome differentiation and treatment of lung precancerous lesions.

articles.titulo: Public preferences for mosquito-borne disease prevention interventions in metropolitan France: a discrete choice experiment.
articles.autores: Dussault J, Ocampo Alvarado JC, … Mueller JE (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Mosquito-borne diseases (MBDs), e.g., dengue, are an emerging public health threat in metropolitan France. While various preventive strategies exist, their real-world success depends on public uptake and adherence. However, research quantifying population preferences for these interventions remains scarce in non-endemic European settings. This study aimed to elicit preferences for key MBD preventive interventions to inform the design of acceptable health policies.
We conducted a cross-sectional online survey in November 2023, recruiting a representative sample of adults aged 18-79 residing in metropolitan France (N = 2,087). We employed a discrete choice experiment (DCE) to elicit preferences. Participants completed ten unlabeled, forced-choice A vs. B tasks, selecting between two hypothetical intervention scenarios defined by four attributes: participation (e.g., government-led vs. individual), intervention frequency, environmental effects, and human health side effects. Average preferences and preference heterogeneity for each MBD attribute were retrieved from mixed multinomial logistic (MMNL) models with correlated random parameters. The drivers of preference heterogeneity were further assessed using interaction effects with respondents' characteristics and simulations were performed to assess optimal interventions that achieved greatest gains in aggregated utility.
All attributes influenced hypothetical decisions. Respondents exhibited the strongest aversion to interventions with systematic negative effects on animals and vegetation (β = -1.77), followed closely by those carrying risks of rare but serious human health side effects (β = -1.48). In terms of governance, government-led implementation was preferred over approaches relying on individual or community compliance. Notably, measures dependent on full community participation were disliked (β = -0.50). While interventions requiring greater time commitment reduced utility (β = -0.22), convenience was a secondary driver compared to health safety. Simulation analysis indicated that installing insect screens yielded the highest predicted utility, while chemical fumigation would generate highest welfare losses.
Public acceptability of MBD prevention in France hinges critically on environmental and health safety rather than convenience. The findings reveal a preference for centralized, government-managed interventions over those requiring coordinated community effort and compliance. To maximize uptake, policymakers should prioritize environmentally safe interventions and adopt transparent communication strategies that directly address public concerns regarding ecological impact and health side effects.

articles.titulo: Metabolism and Metabolomics in Sjögren's Disease.
articles.revista: Rheumatic diseases clinics of North America
articles.autores: Scofield RH, Ice JA (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: While Sjögren's disease (SjD) is a chronic autoimmune disorder marked by lymphocytic infiltration of the salivary and lacrimal glands, profound fatigue represents one of the most significant unmet needs in this disease process. Increasingly, emerging evidence highlights burgeoning roles for immunometabolism not only in lymphocyte activation and differentiation but also in driving mitochondrial dysfunction that contributes to fatigue in related autoimmune conditions like lupus. We outline priority directions for future immunometabolism research efforts in SjD and discuss therapeutic opportunities afforded by emerging insights in the field.

articles.titulo: First molecular detection of haemosporidians in two South American avian species of conservation concern, Crax fasciolata (Galliformes) and Pteroglossus bailloni (Piciformes).
articles.revista: Veterinary parasitology, regional studies and reports
articles.autores: de Rezende MVF, da Silva NM, … D'Agosto M (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Studies on the diversity of haemosporidians infecting larger Neotropical birds classified under vulnerable conservation status remain scarce in the literature. Here, we present the first molecular evidence (cytb) of Plasmodium huffi-like in Pteroglossus bailloni (Piciformes) and Haemoproteus sp. in Crax fasciolata (Galliformes) from the Atlantic Forest, obtained at a Wildlife Triage Center in the municipality of Juiz de Fora, Minas Gerais, Brazil. The three new lineages detected in three individuals of P. bailloni are distinct and clustered within a clade (98% bootstrap support) containing 13 additional lineages of P. huffi and Plasmodium sp., showing low genetic divergence. The new Haemoproteus lineage detected in C. fasciolata (Galliformes) clustered within a clade (99% bootstrap support) containing seven other lineages of Haemoproteus syrnii and Haemoproteus sp.; however, due to the previous taxonomic uncertainty surrounding H. syrnii, we did not assign the new lineage to the species level. The new records of haemosporidians in C. fasciolata (vulnerable) and P. bailloni (near threatened) highlight the need to expand investigations on haemosporidians infecting bird species with some degree of conservation vulnerability and inhabiting landscapes strongly transformed by human activities.

articles.titulo: Caste-specific dynamics of brain biogenic amine levels and physiological states through the life cycle in the giant hornet Vespa mandarinia.
articles.autores: Sasaki K, Nemoto K, Nishimura M (3 autores)
articles.resumo_original: The physiological state of the brain is a crucial factor that influences social behavior and interacts with the condition of peripheral organs. To explore the physiological mechanisms underlying caste-specific behaviors in eusocial wasps, we investigated levels of biogenic amines in the brain, lipid storage and ovarian development in the abdomen at different life stages in each caste of the giant hornet Vespa mandarinia. Gynes had significantly larger thoracic widths and more ovarioles than workers. Maximum oocyte lengths and lipid storage differed plastically between life stages, particularly in gynes. At emergence, significantly higher levels of dopamine-related substances were found in the whole brain of gynes than in workers, whereas levels of serotonin-related substances were higher in workers than in gynes. The levels of these substances differed between life stages in each caste. In queenless workers, maximum oocyte lengths were positively correlated with the levels of dopamine-related substances but not positively correlated with other substances we examined. In gynes, dopamine levels in brain sub-compartments were significantly higher than for workers in several regions except for the optic lobes and varied across life stages. These results suggested that dopamine may be associated with the mating and reproductive behavior in gynes, whereas serotonin may be involved in worker-specific behaviors. The dopamine results indicate convergent caste differentiation in brain physiology between eusocial bees and wasps. Biogenic amine dynamics across the life cycle were caste-specific, suggesting different usage between castes.

articles.titulo: Retrospective analysis of feline heartworm disease (): diagnostic patterns in cats presenting with respiratory or vomiting signs (2013-2023, USA).
articles.autores: Whittle A, Ferguson B, … Mwacalimba K (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Feline heartworm infection, caused by the mosquito-borne nematode Dirofilaria immitis, is a serious and potentially fatal disease in cats. The true prevalence of this infection is likely underestimated due to the nonspecific nature of clinical signs, such as coughing, vomiting, or respiratory distress, and the diagnostic limitations of current feline heartworm antigen (Ag) and antibody (Ab) assays. This study aimed to enhance understanding of its recognition and detection by linking diverse clinical presentations with diagnostic test results. Anonymized feline medical records spanning 10 years from more than 1,000 Banfield U.S. veterinary clinics were analyzed using machine learning methods. Cats were included if records contained respiratory, vomiting, or heartworm-specific diagnostic codes and at least one heartworm Ag or Ab test. Test positivity rates were linked to clinical signs. For cats tested with both assays, concordance between results was assessed. Of 146,111 eligible cats, 91,438 (62.58%) underwent heartworm testing, and 1,555 (1.70%) were positive on at least one assay. Cats with heartworm-specific diagnostic codes had the highest positivity, but those with respiratory or vomiting codes accounted for 7.01 and 10.10% of all positives. Among 127 cats tested with both assays, 24.41% were discordant, mainly Ag-positive/Ab-negative. Heartworm infection should be considered in any cat with respiratory signs (including asthma-like presentations) or vomiting. To improve its detection, both heat-treated Ag and Ab assays should be used to screen cats annually, and in cats presenting with respiratory signs or vomiting.

articles.titulo: New medium for the production of Dermacentor reticulatus and Ixodes persulcatus tick primary cell lines
articles.autores: Ananko GG, K. AV (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Background. The increasing prevalence of diseases caused by vector borne infections is an important public health problem. Currently, over 1000 extant tick species have been identified worldwide, and approximately ten percent of them are known to be vectors of pathogens (protozoa, bacteria, and viruses), leading to diseases in animals and humans. Tick cell lines are increasingly being used in research on tick physiology and the pathogens of vector borne infections. To obtain and maintain tick cell lines, traditionally used L-15-based nutrient media. However, obtaining a continuous tick cell line remains a complex and time consuming process. Therefore, it is important to develop new methods that can accelerate the process of obtaining tick cell cultures. Methods. To establish primary tick cell lines, we used, for the first time, a ready-made DMEM/F12 + GlutaMAX culture medium supplemented with 20% fetal bovine serum. Results. In this study, it was shown that DMEM/F12 + GlutaMAX nutrient medium is suitable for obtaining primary cell cultures of two species of ticks from two different genera of the family Ixodidae. Primary cell lines of the tick Ixodes persulcatus were obtained for the first time. We also managed to accelerate the process of obtaining subcultures: the first subcultures were obtained within 1-2 months of tick tissue isolation. Conclusions. This new method, allows us to overcome several existing technical difficulties. It is likely that the DMEM/F12 + Glutamax medium can also be used to obtain and maintain tick cell lines of other species. Thus, an alternative to the traditionally used L-15-based media has emerged, allowing researchers to select the medium most suitable for their tasks. The rapid production of subcultures creates opportunities to conduct certain studies directly on primary cultures, without waiting for their transformation into an immortal culture.

articles.titulo: Automated detection and classification of morphologically similar weevil species using AI for precision pest monitoring
articles.autores: Tukuli AR et al. (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Accurate identification of morphologically similar insects is important for agricultural surveillance but remains challenging when large and balanced image datasets are limited. We developed Rostrum Recognition: A Weevil Identification Tool (RRWIT), a lightweight object-detection framework for distinguishing 14 weevil taxa, including two economically important weevil species, the boll weevil and pecan weevil, using more than 16,000 expert-verified annotated images. RRWIT was developed by transfer learning from a pretrained YOLO11n detector using a stratified data partition with the test set withheld from model and threshold selection. We evaluated this design with matched random-initialization and transfer-learning experiments, quantitative EigenGradCAM attribution analysis, targeted architectural modifications, and a frozen eight-framework benchmark across three independent training seeds. In the cross-framework benchmark, RRWIT achieved a mean average precision at an intersection-over-union threshold of 0.50 (mAP50) of 0.938 {+/-} 0.005 on held-out test partitions subset, whereas the newer lightweight YOLO26n achieved the highest value, 0.976 {+/-} 0.010, with a similarly compact computational footprint. Post-training 8-bit integer (INT8) quantization reduced the serialized RRWIT model from 10.09 to 2.91 MiB (71.2%) with a small validation mAP50 change from 0.978 to 0.971 but did not accelerate end-to-end inference under the tested central processing unit configuration. RRWIT therefore provides an extensible foundation for automated weevil identification while highlighting the importance of representative biological data, independent external validation, evolving lightweight architectures, and hardware-specific deployment optimization in future development. A publicly accessible RRWIT web application supporting image upload and live image capture for automated weevil detection and classification is available at https://huggingface.co/spaces/adamartukuli/RRWIT.

articles.titulo: Stannous Fluoride Deposition Into Plaque Biofilm: Effects of Formulation Chemistry and Hops β-Acids Extract Dispersion.
articles.revista: Compendium of continuing education in dentistry (Jamesburg, N.J. : 1995)
articles.autores: St John S, Strand R (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
To evaluate how surfactant-mediated biofilm disruption by hops beta (β)-acids extract influences stannous fluoride (SnF2) penetration and interaction with extracellular metabolites, including lipopolysaccharide (LPS).
In two studies, oral biofilms were formed in vivo on artificial enamel surfaces mounted in dental appliances worn by volunteers and subsequently treated ex vivo under controlled conditions. Across the studies, biofilms were treated with supernatants of various commercial 0.454% SnF2 dentifrices containing: (1) pyrophosphate; (2) potassium nitrate (KNO3) and pyrophosphate; (3) tripolyphosphate; and (4) gluconate/citrate-stabilized 0.454% SnF2 (Crest) with and without hops β-acids extract (Activ Bio-Cleanser™). Both studies used phosphate-buffered saline as a negative control (NC). Confocal laser scanning microscopy with component-specific fluorescent probes was used to quantify Sn and LPS distribution relative to bacterial biomass, biofilm thickness, and extracellular polymeric substance (EPS) structure. Image analysis was used to quantify Sn and LPS signal within bacterial regions, normalized to bacterial volume or area; statistical comparisons were made across conditions.
SnF2 uptake and penetration varied significantly across formulations. In study 1, the rank order from greatest to least for Sn deposition and LPS neutralization was: gluconate/citrate > KNO3 + pyro > pyro > NC (P < 0.05 between groups). In study 2, the rank order from greatest to least was: gluconate/citrate + hops > gluconate/citrate > tripolyphosphate and KNO3 + pyro > NC (P < 0.05 between groups). Some stabilized SnF2 systems exhibited limited penetration, consistent with diffusion barriers imposed by dense EPS matrices or over-stabilization reducing bioavailability. Gluconate/ citrate-stabilized SnF2-only treated biofilms showed higher deposition per unit bacteria than other SnF2 technologies but uniformly exhibited the majority of uptake in surface regions. In the formulation containing both hops and SnF2, increased Sn penetration and reduced detectable biofilm-associated LPS was observed, consistent with enhanced access of SnF2 to extracellular plaque components following surfactant-enabled biofilm modification. In this case, Sn penetration achieved high relative deposition per unit bacteria in the treated regions throughout the biofilm.
Hops β-acids extract acts as a co-surfactant in toothpaste, capable of modifying EPS structure to improve accessibility and interaction of SnF2 with extracellular metabolites within oral biofilms. The observed changes in Sn penetration and biofilm-associated, extracellular LPS are consistent with enhanced cleaning with reduced concentration of known tissue irritants.
These findings provide a mechanistic rationale for formulation strategies that enhance SnF2 accessibility within adherent oral biofilms through surfactant-based modification of EPS supporting more efficient biofilm management during oral hygiene and providing a basis for selecting toothpastes based on their efficacy.

articles.titulo: Update on the Malaria Situation in the Americas, 2015 - 2024.
articles.autores: Navarro-Costa D, Araújo RM (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Malaria remains a major Public Health challenge in the Americas despite the recent certification of several countries as malaria-free. This regional analysis describes malaria trends from 2015 to 2024, identifies populations and territories with the highest burden, and examines opportunities to accelerate elimination. National and subnational surveillance data reported by countries were analyzed by parasite species, mortality, population group, geographic concentration, and access to diagnosis and treatment. Reported cases increased by 9% between 2015 and 2024, from 488,227 to 536,664, whereas malaria deaths declined by 20%, from 169 to 136. Plasmodium vivax remained predominant, but P. falciparum cases increased by 42.4%, from 102,304 to 145,440, and represented 30% of regional cases in 2024. Indigenous populations accounted for 35% of cases and 27% of malaria deaths in 2024, and transmission remained highly concentrated in a small number of municipalities, particularly in the Amazon, the Guiana Shield, the Colombian Pacific, Haiti, and Eastern Panama. Mining, agricultural labor, population mobility, geographic isolation, and delayed access to diagnosis and treatment were recurrent determinants. Rapid diagnostic tests remained underused in several high-burden countries. Achieving elimination will require expanded and decentralized access to diagnosis and immediate treatment, intensified subnational surveillance and response, improved radical cure of P. vivax, and accelerated elimination of P. falciparum before antimalarial resistance emerges or spreads.

articles.titulo: Blood Feeding Modulates Lysophospholipid Acyltransferase Gene Expression Along the Gut of Rhodnius prolixus.
articles.revista: Archives of insect biochemistry and physiology
articles.autores: Braz V, Araujo MFC, … C Atella G (4 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Lysophosphatidylcholine (LPC) is a bioactive lipid at the interface between the triatomine Rhodnius prolixus and Trypanosoma cruzi. The phospholipases A2 that generate LPC have been studied in this vector, but the lysophospholipid acyltransferases (LPLATs) that consume it in the Lands' cycle have not been described in any triatomine species. We characterized the domain architecture of the four LPLATs encoded by the R. prolixus genome and measured their transcript abundance by RT-qPCR in the anterior midgut, posterior midgut and hindgut of females before and up to 15 days after a blood meal. Three genes encode polytopic membrane-bound O-acyltransferase (MBOAT) proteins orthologous to the Drosophila enzymes Oysgedart (human MBOAT1/2), Nessy (LPCAT3) and Farjavit (MBOAT7); the fourth combines an AGPAT-type acyltransferase domain with two EF-hand motifs, the architecture of LPCAT1. Transcription was regulated in a gene-, time- and region-specific manner. RpFarjavit was modulated in all three gut regions and was induced about eightfold in the hindgut on Day 3 post-feeding. In the posterior midgut, RpNessy and RpFarjavit were repressed on Days 3-7 and induced on Day 10 post-feeding, when this organ becomes the main site of lipid uptake. RpLPCAT1 was not modulated. The LPC-consuming arm of the Lands' cycle is present in R. prolixus and is coupled to the digestive cycle in the gut compartments where T. cruzi develops.

v6.implicacao: Alimentação sanguínea de Aedes / Imunometabolismo: curva de lisofosfolipídio/Lands cycle ao longo do intestino após o repasto, do tipo que se poderia medir em Aedes sob repasto HFHS.
v6.resumo: Em Rhodnius prolixus, quatro aciltransferases de lisofosfolipídio (Lands cycle) tiveram expressão regulada por gene, tempo e região do intestino após o repasto; RpFarjavit subiu cerca de oito vezes no intestino posterior no dia 3, e RpNessy e RpFarjavit foram reprimidos nos dias 3 a 7 e induzidos no dia 10 no intestino médio posterior, quando ele vira o sítio principal de captação de lipídio.
v6.metodo: RT-qPCR em intestino médio anterior, posterior e reto de fêmeas antes e até 15 dias após o repasto; análise de domínios das proteínas.

articles.titulo: Multistage Insecticidal Activity of Juniperus phoenicea Essential Oil Against Culex pipiens, a Major West Nile Virus Vector: Biochemical and Histopathological Effects, Molecular Docking, and Non-target Selectivity.
articles.autores: Madani F, Haleche I, … Tail G (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Given the need for environmentally sustainable alternatives for mosquito control, this study aimed to assess the biocidal potential of Juniperus phoenicea essential oil (EC) against developmental stages of Culex pipiens, a major vector of West Nile virus and other pathogens, while elucidating its biochemical and histopathological effects, interactions with acetylcholinesterase (AChE), and effects on two non-target aquatic organisms, Daphnia magna and Cloeon dipterum.
Egg-hatching inhibition, larvicidal, and pupicidal bioassays were conducted to determine IC₅₀ and LC₅₀ values, as appropriate. The chemical composition of the essential oil (EO) was characterized using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS). Changes in protein, carbohydrate, and lipid contents, as well as histopathological alterations in the midgut, were assessed. Molecular docking was performed to investigate the potential interactions of all identified EO constituents with AChE. The toxicity of EO to D. magna and C. dipterum was also evaluated.
GC-MS analysis identified 101 compounds, with α-pinene (21.12%), trans-calamene (4.87%), and 1,10-di-epi-cubenol (3.69%) as the predominant constituents. The EO inhibited egg hatching and exhibited larvicidal and pupicidal activities, with an IC50 of 130.4 µL/L for egg-hatching inhibition and LC50 values of 56.15 and 107.2 µL/L for larvae and pupae, respectively. Larvae exhibited the lowest LC50 among the tested life stages. Exposure induced metabolic disturbances and marked midgut alterations. Manooloxide showed the most favorable predicted binding energy for AChE (- 8.2 kcal/mol). In D. magna, mortality remained below 30% at the tested concentrations, whereas no mortality was observed in C. dipterum.
To our knowledge, this study provides the first integrated assessment of J. phoenicea essential oil against the egg, larval, and pupal stages of C. pipiens, integrating biochemical and histopathological analyses with molecular docking predictions involving AChE and an assessment of toxicity to non-target aquatic organisms. Its activity across multiple developmental stages and the limited mortality observed in the tested non-target species suggest potential for further investigation as a botanical insecticide for integrated vector management, pending further evaluation of its ecological safety and selectivity.

articles.titulo: PDE4B Inhibition Attenuates Intestinal Inflammation with Reducing Glycolysis in Macrophages.
articles.autores: Mao H, Lu Y, … Wang Y (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Accumulating evidence underscores that PDE4B expression is significantly upregulated in patients with inflammatory bowel disease (IBD). However, its therapeutic potential and the underlying molecular mechanisms in pediatric IBD remain poorly defined. In this study, multiple public datasets were analyzed to characterize PDE4B expression in pediatric IBD. This was followed by therapeutic evaluation in mice colitis models to validate the efficacy of PDE4B inhibition in vivo. Analysis of public datasets revealed a marked elevation of PDE4B in pediatric IBD cohorts. Mechanistically, we demonstrated that a PDE4B inhibitor effectively suppressed LPS-induced inflammatory responses in primary blood samples from pediatric patients. In murine models, pharmacological inhibition of PDE4B significantly attenuated intestinal inflammation in both DSS- and LPS-induced colitis models. Furthermore, treatment with the PDE4B inhibitor successfully alleviated established chronic mucosal injury and preserved goblet cell integrity in spontaneous Il10-/- mice. Furthermore, 16S rRNA gene sequencing demonstrated that PDE4B inhibition was associated with a partial restoration of gut microbiota diversity and a reduction in specific bacterial dysbiosis. At the molecular level, the inhibitor promoted the activation of the anti-inflammatory mediator p-CREB while concurrently abrogating pro-inflammatory p-STAT3 signaling. Notably, the suppression of pathological glycolysis by the inhibitor was closely accompanied by the metabolic reprogramming and enhanced anti-inflammatory function. In conclusion, these findings suggest that targeting PDE4B represents a potential therapeutic approach for pediatric IBD by modulating macrophage immunometabolism and restoring intestinal homeostasis.

articles.titulo: Native architecture of a mitochondrial oxphosome
articles.autores: Melnik M et al. (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Mitochondrial cristae are the primary bioenergetic units of eukaryotic cells, yet the molecular principles that dictate their morphologies remain largely unknown. Using in situ cryo-electron tomography and integrative modeling, we resolve the native organization of the respiratory machinery in the diatom Phaeodactylum tricornutum. Unlike previously studied animals and green algae, diatoms possess tubular crista, a conserved membrane architecture found in diverse and globally relevant species. We identify several native supercomplexes assemblies, including an oxphosome comprising the entire respiratory chain. Our results, together with molecular dynamics analyses, reveal that these supercomplexes assemble through a lipid-mediated mechanism. We propose that tubular cristae are shaped by the interplay between membrane-bending ATP synthase oligomers that bud the hemispherical crista tips and supercomplexes that act as molecular roadblocks to constrain ATP synthase propagation, thereby balancing membrane curvature and allowing cristae body extension. Furthermore, we show that the diatom Complex I retains ancestral subunits related to fatty acid synthase. Beyond illuminating diatom bioenergetics, our findings reveal a fundamental principle of mitochondrial morphogenesis where ATP synthase-driven membrane curvature is spatially fine-tuned by respiratory supercomplexes.

articles.titulo: Comparative effectiveness of tirzepatide versus GLP-1 receptor agonists on the risk of incident infection and severe infection-related outcomes in type 2 diabetes.
articles.autores: Wu JY, Lee KW, … Lin YM (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Patients with type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM) are at increased risk of infection-related morbidity and mortality. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1RAs) may exert immunomodulatory effects beyond glycemic control. Tirzepatide, a dual glucose-dependent insulinotropic peptide and GLP-1 receptor agonist, has demonstrated superior metabolic efficacy, but its association with infection-related outcomes remains unclear.
We conducted a retrospective cohort study using the TriNetX research network including adults with T2DM between January 2022 and November 2025. New users of tirzepatide were compared with new users of GLP-1RAs. Propensity score matching (1:1) balanced demographic characteristics, comorbidities, medications, and laboratory variables. The primary endpoint was a composite of infection-related events within 1 year. Secondary outcomes included pneumonia, skin infection, and all-cause mortality. Cox proportional hazards models were used to estimate hazard ratios (HRs).
After matching, 143,288 patients were included in each group. Tirzepatide initiation was associated with a modestly lower risk of composite infection-related events compared with GLP-1RAs (HR 0.97, 95% CI 0.95-0.99). Lower risks were observed for pneumonia (HR 0.95, 95% CI 0.92-0.98), skin infection (HR 0.96, 95% CI 0.93-0.99), and all-cause mortality (HR 0.89, 95% CI 0.82-0.98). Results were consistent across most prespecified subgroups and sensitivity analyses, including landmark analyses and a negative control outcome. No significant differences were observed for acute pyelonephritis or gastrointestinal infection.
In this large real-world cohort of patients with T2DM, tirzepatide use was associated with a modestly lower risk of infection-related outcomes compared with GLP-1RAs. These findings suggest that dual GIP/GLP-1 receptor agonism may be associated with differences in infection-related outcomes, although prospective studies are needed to confirm causality.

articles.titulo: Geospatial risk mapping and time-series forecasting of malaria transmission among under-fives in Bauchi and Oyo States, Nigeria.
articles.autores: Nkeiruka OJ, Taiwo OJ, … Kaduru C (10 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Malaria remains a major public health challenge in Nigeria, with marked geographic and seasonal variability influencing transmission dynamics. Understanding spatial and temporal heterogeneity is essential for optimising malaria control strategies and improving the targeting of interventions. This study investigated under-five malaria transmission patterns in two epidemiologically distinct Nigerian states using integrated time-series forecasting and Bayesian geospatial risk mapping.
A two-stage analytical framework was applied to monthly confirmed under-five malaria cases obtained from the District Health Information System 2 (DHIS2) between January 2014 and December 2024. At the state level, autoregressive integrated moving average models with exogenous variables (ARIMAX) were developed using climatic variables obtained from the NASA Prediction of Worldwide Energy Resources (POWER) database. Candidate lag structures were identified using cross-correlation analysis, and competing models were compared using the Akaike Information Criterion (AIC), Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), Mean Absolute Error (MAE), and Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE). Final models were validated using out-of-sample data before generating forecasts for January-December 2025. At the Local Government Area (LGA) level, Bayesian Besag-York-Mollié (BYM) models were used to estimate annual relative malaria risk.
Bauchi exhibited a substantially higher malaria burden and stronger seasonal transmission than Oyo throughout the study period. One-month lagged rainfall improved forecasting performance in both states, whereas temperature did not improve predictive accuracy and was excluded from the final models. Forecasts for 2025 projected continued seasonal transmission, with substantially higher malaria incidence in Bauchi than in Oyo. Bayesian spatial analysis identified persistent high-risk LGAs in Bauchi, particularly Warji, despite declining risk over time, while Ido remained the principal persistent hotspot in Oyo.
Integrating ARIMAX forecasting with Bayesian geospatial risk mapping provides a comprehensive framework for characterising malaria transmission dynamics and identifying persistent transmission hotspots. The findings highlight the value of combining routine surveillance data with climate information to strengthen malaria early warning systems and support geographically targeted malaria control strategies in Nigeria.
Not applicable.

articles.titulo: Peripheral and Uterine NK Cell Immunometabolic Concordance: A Minimally Invasive Approach to Endometrial Receptivity Assessment.
articles.revista: American journal of reproductive immunology (New York, N.Y. : 1989)
articles.autores: Celik O, Celik S (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Recurrent implantation failure (RIF) occurs even after euploid embryo transfer, indicating a maternal determinant beyond embryo quality. A landmark meta-analysis showed that peripheral NK (pNK) cell numbers do not correlate with endometrial NK (uNK) cell numbers and called for functional rather than numerical assessment.
Narrative synthesis of immunometabolism, reproductive immunology, endometrial tissue metabolism, and uterine luminal sampling evidence to develop a testable model.
We propose that pNK cells may exhibit immunometabolic states correlated with, but not identical to, those of endometrial uNK cells (immunometabolic concordance). Concordance does not imply functional equivalence: pNK cells are predominantly cytotoxic, whereas uNK cells are angiogenic and immunomodulatory. We propose three axes, ΔΨm, mtROS, and intracellular lipid load, as measurable determinants of uNK function. Among minimally invasive routes, uterine luminal fluid currently has the most direct feasibility evidence, whereas cervical mucus remains hypothesis-generating and unproven. Assay-specific confounders, including P-glycoprotein-mediated dye efflux, are explicitly addressed. Six testable predictions and a prospective validation protocol are presented.
If validated, the model could reduce reliance on endometrial biopsy; if not, it will show that functional NK assessment requires compartment-specific analysis.

articles.titulo: Screening of open-source libraries from the Medicines for Malaria Venture using Bunyamwera virus as a model reveals inhibitors of Oropouche virus infection.
articles.autores: Cassani NM, Pearson HM, … Jardim ACG (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Arboviral infections remain a major public health concern in tropical and subtropical regions, where environmental and socioeconomic conditions facilitate the circulation of diverse RNA viruses, including over 350 members of the recently renamed Peribunyaviridae family. In this regard, Oropouche virus (OROV) has caused explosive outbreaks in the Amazon region and shows wider distribution in Brazil, with confirmed neurological infections and fatalities in 2024. The absence of effective antiviral therapies highlights an urgent need for the discovery of anti-OROV drugs. In this work, we evaluated the antiviral potential of the Pandemic Response Box and Global Health Priority Box libraries from the Medicines for Malaria Venture (MMV) against OROV, using a well-established Bunyamwera virus (BUNV) system, widely used as a prototype of the Peribunyaviridae family, expressing the reporter gene enhanced green fluorescent protein (eGFP). A screening protocol based on fluorescent reporter gene detection by live cell imaging was employed. Nine compounds were identified with significant activity against BUNV-eGFP, with three being highlighted as the most promising hits: Trimetrexate, GSK-983 and MMV1634385. These compounds were validated by testing for activity against OROV, and in these assays, GSK-983 exhibited the lowest EC50 value and consequently the highest selectivity index. Future studies should evaluate the antiviral efficacy of GSK-983 and assess its pharmacokinetic profile. Furthermore, our results indicate that our approach employing BUNV-eGFP as a model against OROV provides an efficient route to prioritize candidate compounds from large libraries, thereby establishing a practical screening route for future antivirals against Oropouche fever.

articles.titulo: Spatiotemporal epidemiology of dengue fever across all 64 districts of Bangladesh: a retrospective ecological analysis of reported hospital admissions.
articles.autores: Nabed IA, Daiby AT, … Hayat T (5 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Bangladesh has experienced increasingly widespread dengue activity, with hospital admissions reported beyond the historical concentration in Dhaka. District-level evidence is needed to support preparedness, but nationwide-analyses combining temporal patterns, population-standardised reported admission rates, and spatial clustering remain limited.
We conducted a retrospective ecological spatiotemporal analysis of reported dengue hospital admissions across all 64 districts of Bangladesh using daily Directorate General of Health Services Health Emergency Operations Centre reports from 1 January 2022 to 31 December 2025. The analytical dataset contained 93,504 district-day observations after imputing 19 missing dates using district-wise linear interpolation. Annual reported admission rates per 100,000 population were computed using district mid-year population projections from the 2022 census. Temporal patterns were assessed descriptively, with exploratory Seasonal Mann-Kendall assessment and Benjamini-Hochberg false-discovery-rate correction. Spatial clustering was evaluated using Global Moran's I, Local Indicators of Spatial Association (LISA), and Getis-Ord Gi* under queen-contiguity weights, with K-nearest-neighbour (k = 6) sensitivity analysis. Additional sensitivity analyses examined the impact of missing-date handling.
DGHS yearly totals reported 62,382 dengue admissions in 2022, 321,017 in 2023, 101,214 in 2024, and 102,861 in 2025. Corresponding totals in the interpolated dataset were 62,034, 320,943, 100,803, and 102,929, respectively, reflecting minor differences attributable to interpolation of missing dates. Reported admissions increased sharply from 2022 to 2023, declined substantially in 2024, and remained stable in 2025. Dhaka district's share of national admissions fell from 63.5% to 31.5% between 2022 and 2025, while Barishal Division's share increased from 5.1% to 21.1%. In 2025, Barguna recorded the highest reported admission rate (959.5 per 100,000 population). Spatial autocorrelation was strongest from 2023 onward, with weak positive autocorrelation detected in 2022. Dhaka was not identified as a statistically significant LISA or Gi* hotspot core, unlike spatially coherent southern clusters emerging 2023 onwards.
Reported dengue hospital admissions show an apparent redistribution beyond Dhaka, with repeated concentration in several southern districts after 2023. Because the analysis is based on hospital-reported admissions, a study-period of four years, and facility-location rather than residence-location data, the findings should be interpreted as suggestive evidence of changing dengue-admission patterns.

articles.titulo: LC-MS-Based Chlorine-Signature Query Engine Strategy for Automated Discovery of Phosphate-Containing Metabolites.
articles.autores: Chen X, Li Y, … Wu JL (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Comprehensive profiling of phosphate-containing compounds (PCCs) in untargeted metabolomics remains challenging due to their high hydrophilicity, poor separation, and low stability, which hampers high-throughput screening from large-scale liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry (LC-MS) datasets. Herein, an LC-MS-based chlorine-tagging strategy integrated with a Chlorine Signature Query Engine (Cl-SQE) was established for the rapid identification of potential PCCs in complex matrices. The novel derivatization reagent, [5-(2-chlorophenyl)isoxazol-3-yl]methyl amine (ClXIMA), can react with phosphate groups on PCCs, such as nucleotides, sugar phosphates, glycerophosphates, and nucleotide sugars under mild conditions, thereby markedly enhancing reversed-phase retention and separation resolution. More importantly, the incorporation of chlorine, identifiable by its characteristic isotopic peak pattern, provides a unique digital signature in the mass spectra. Leveraging these features, Cl-SQE, a data mining program, was developed to systematically and automatically extract candidate PCCs from large-scale datasets. By applying this strategy to liver tissues from a mouse model of cholestasis, 318 potential ClXIMA derivatives were screened out, and 189 metabolites were identified or tentatively assigned. Statistical analysis revealed significant disturbances in nucleotide metabolism, addressing a critical gap in phospho-metabolomic profiling for cholestatic disease and revealing dysregulated nucleotide homeostasis as a potential feature of cholestasis-associated metabolic remodeling. Overall, this platform facilitates the discovery of PCCs in complex matrices and provides new insights into the pathogenesis of cholestasis and other clinical diseases.

articles.titulo: Immunomodulatory Effects of Dodelate C against Plasmodium by Reshaping Macrophage Function.
articles.autores: Wu J, Cang LQ, … Jiang B (6 autores)
articles.resumo_original: This study investigated the effect and molecular mechanism of Dodelate C, a sesquiterpenoid isolated from Dobinea delavayi, in regulating macrophage function during malaria. Its antiplasmodial activity was tested in vitro against Plasmodium falciparum 3D7, and macrophage regulatory effects examined in vivo in Plasmodium yoelii-infected mice. Cytokine levels were quantified by enzyme-linked immunosorbent assay (ELISA); macrophage polarization was analyzed via flow cytometry, with proliferation and phagocytosis measured by Cell Counting Kit-8 (CCK-8) and neutral red uptake assays. Network pharmacology, molecular docking, and dynamics simulations identified potential targets, with key protein expression validated by Western blot. Dodelate C exerted robust antiplasmodial activity both in vitro and in vivo. In infected mice, it significantly reduced serum interferon-gamma (IFN-γ) and nitric oxide (NO) levels, increased total macrophages, and markedly decreased the M1/M2 ratio. At non-cytotoxic concentrations in RAW 264.7 cells, Dodelate C enhanced macrophage phagocytic function and regulated macrophage polarization: it downregulated CD86 and pro-inflammatory factors (NO, tumor necrosis factor-alpha [TNF-α], and interleukin-1 beta [IL-1β]) to suppress the M1 phenotype, while upregulating CD206 and interleukin-10 (IL-10) to promote M2. Additionally, Dodelate C elevated Beclin-1 and the microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3 (LC3)-II/LC3-I ratio, modulating peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor (PPAR) and phosphoinositide 3-kinase/protein kinase B (PI3K/Akt) signaling by upregulating PPARγ/retinoid X receptor alpha (RXRα) and reducing insulin-like growth factor 1 receptor (IGF1R)/Akt/mammalian target of rapamycin (mTOR) phosphorylation. These findings show Dodelate C modulates macrophage function by balancing polarization and regulating autophagy, driving its antimalarial efficacy.

articles.titulo: Ferroptosis as an Immunometabolic Regulator in Autoimmune Diseases: Mechanisms, Biomarkers, and Therapeutic Implications.
articles.autores: Ahmed Z, B H (2 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
Autoimmune diseases involve persistent immune dysregulation, oxidative stress, and progressive tissue injury. Ferroptosis, an iron-dependent form of regulated cell death driven by lipid peroxidation and impaired antioxidant defences, may contribute to these processes.
This review examines the immunological relevance of ferroptosis in autoimmune diseases, focusing on iron homeostasis, lipid peroxidation, GPX4 (glutathione peroxidase 4), system xc- (cystine/glutamate antiporter), inflammatory pathways, immune-cell dysfunction, biomarkers, and therapeutic strategies.
Ferroptosis has been implicated in synovial inflammation and fibroblast-like synoviocyte dysfunction in rheumatoid arthritis, and in neutrophil abnormalities, oxidative injury, and lupus nephritis in systemic lupus erythematosus. Related mechanisms are also being explored in multiple sclerosis, inflammatory bowel disease, and other autoimmune conditions.
Ferroptosis may represent a shared but context-dependent immunometabolic process in autoimmunity, with potential diagnostic and therapeutic relevance. However, disease heterogeneity, cell-specific effects, limited human validation, and the need for biomarker-guided precision approaches remain important challenges.

articles.titulo: A multipathogen view of Epstein-Barr virus pathogenesis and tumorigenesis.
articles.autores: Tang J, Zhong L, … Zhang X (7 autores)
articles.resumo_original: Epstein-Barr virus (EBV) infects more than 95% of the global population and contributes to multiple human cancers and autoimmune diseases. Co-infection with pathogens including Helicobacter pylori, human immunodeficiency virus, human papillomavirus, and Plasmodium falciparum can reshape host immunity and the EBV latency-lytic balance and, in some settings, promote reactivation. Collectively, these interactions may exacerbate chronic inflammation, immunosuppression, and epigenetic dysregulation to accelerate disease progression and tumor formation. Existing clinical treatments control only the active pathogens but fail to target latent EBV. Emerging strategies such as clustered regularly interspaced short palindromic repeats (CRISPR) gene editing and EBV-targeted immunotherapy aim to eliminate latent viral reservoirs. This review outlines the synergistic mechanisms of EBV co-infection in oncogenesis, highlighting that further research on pathogen interactions is vital for developing better prevention and treatment options.

articles.titulo: Distribution of kdr-west and kdr-east resistance alleles in Anopheles gambiae s.l. across contrasting transmission settings in central and southern Senegal.
articles.autores: Diop M, Diagne NS, … Niang EHA (25 autores)
articles.resumo_original:
The effectiveness of malaria vector control in sub-Saharan Africa is increasingly threatened by insecticide resistance in Anopheles gambiae sensu lato (s.l.). Knockdown resistance (kdr) mutations L1014F (kdr-west) and L1014S (kdr-east) are key target-site mechanisms associated with resistance to pyrethroids, the primary insecticide class currently approved for long-lasting insecticidal nets. This study assessed insecticide susceptibility and compared the distribution and phenotypic associations of kdr-west and kdr-east mutations in An. gambiae s.l. populations from two health districts in Senegal.
Larvae were collected from four sites in Nioro and Velingara health districts and reared to adulthood. Adult females (3-5 days old) were tested against permethrin, deltamethrin, alphacypermethrin, bendiocarb, and pirimiphos-methyl using WHO susceptibility assays. Molecular identification of sibling species and detection of kdr mutations were performed by PCR. Allelic frequencies were compared between sites and species, and associations between kdr alleles and pyrethroid resistance phenotypes were assessed using odds ratios.
Populations of An. gambiae s.l. from both districts exhibited high resistance to permethrin (9.18%; 13.08%), deltamethrin (46.08%; 48.08%) and alphacypermethrin (75%; 56%) in Nioro and Velingara, respectively. While remaining fully susceptible to bendiocarb (99.06%; 100%) and pirimiphos-methyl (100%; 100%) in Nioro and Velingara, respectively. Anopheles arabiensis was the predominant species in both districts, with higher proportions of An. gambiae sensu stricto (s.s.) and An. coluzzii in Velingara. A total of 85 and 90 An. gambiae s.l. specimens were genotyped to determine kdr-west and kdr-east alleles frequencies, respectively in Nioro and Velingara. Both kdr-west and kdr-east alleles were detected, with marked spatial and species-specific variation. The kdr-west allele was significantly associated with pyrethroid resistance in both Nioro (OR = 5.68, p < 0.01) and Velingara (OR = 2.81, p < 0.01), indicating that mosquitoes carrying kdr-west allele are more likely to survive exposure to pyrethroids than those that do not carry it. Whereas no significant association was observed for the kdr-east allele.
Pyrethroid resistance is widespread in An. gambiae s.l. populations from central and southern Senegal and is significantly associated with the kdr-west mutation. The limited association between kdr-east and resistance phenotypes suggests the involvement of additional resistance mechanisms. These findings highlight the need for resistance-informed vector control strategies and support the integration of complementary interventions in areas with high pyrethroid resistance.
